newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Midwest direct hogs steady-up $1 - dealers.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Midwest direct hogs steady-up $1 - dealers.

text.p: U.S. Midwest direct cash hog prices early Thursday were steady to $1.00 per cwt higher as packers continued to compete for tight hog supplies, livestock dealers said.
Interior Iowa and southern Minnesota hogs sold steady at $55.50 to $56.50 in the country and $57.00 to $58.00 at plants but could turn higher if marketings remain tight, they said.

Illinois hogs sold $0.50 to $1.00 higher at $56.50 to $57.50 in the country and $58.00 to $58.50 at plants. Some packers offered premiums $0.50 to $1.00 above $58.50 for top quality hogs, several dealers in Illinois said.
Indiana hogs sold $0.50 to $1.00 higher at $56.50 to $57.00 in the country and $58.00 to $58.50 at plants.
"Everybody seems a little short on hogs," one Indiana dealer said.
Ohio hogs sold $0.50 higher at $54.50 to $55.00 in the country and $56.50 to $57.50 at plants.
Cash hog prices also were buoyed by gains in pork prices, the dealers said.
Estimated gross cutout values of a 175-lb hog carcass based on cutting yield tests and carlot prices Wednesday were quoted up $1.43 to $1.44 per cwt, USDA reported.
